newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to buy back shares from British Airways.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to buy back shares from British Airways.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc. said Tuesday it will repurchase most of its preferred stock held by British Airways Plc in a move that would end the turbulent four-year relationship between the two carriers.

British Airways, which invested about $400 million in US Airways in 1993, said in December that it planned to sell its 24.6 percent stake in its U.S. marketing partner. The three British Airways representatives on US Airways' board resigned in January.
The relationship between the two carriers began to sour last summer after British Airways proposed a broad alliance with American Airlines, which is owned by Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR Corp.

US Airways sued British Airways in July, alleging that the deal with American undermined US Airways' relationship with the British carrier and could create a monopoly of air travel between the key trans-Atlantic route between the United States and Britain.

Arlington, Va.-based US Airways said in February that it would not exercise its right to buy back British Airways' stake, but it changed tack on Tuesday, saying it can now meet the capital surplus requirements to repurchase them.

"We see this as a very attractive opportunity to purchase stock at a discount to current markets," said Stephen Wolf, US Airways' chairman. "We will continue to seek opportunities to use the company's resources to increase value for our shareholders."

US Airways said it will repurchase and retire most of the preferred stock held by the British carrier. British Airways has agreed to convert the remaining preferred stock it holds into common stock in June.
Analysts said the stock repurchase does not affect the lawsuit, which is still pending. US Airways would not comment on the lawsuit.
US Airways stock was 37.5 cents higher at $35.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
